author: Jesse Garcia
title: Andrew Alvarez K's 6 in 4.2 scoreless for win vs. Boston
desc: Andrew Alvarez allowed zero earned runs on two hits and one walk while striking out six over 4.2 innings in Wednesday's win over the Red Sox.
impact: After the win, Alvarez now has a 2-1 record with a 3.05 ERA and 1.38 WHIP through 11 games. The Nationals used an opener this time in front of Alvarez, so they may choose to continue to operate with that plan in his next outing.

author: Jesse Garcia
title: Nasim Nunez Finally Finds Some Pop in 10-2 Rout
desc: Nasim Nunez went 1-for-4 in a win over the Red Sox with a home run, a walk, a run scored, one RBI, and three strikeouts.
impact: After Wednesday's win, Nunez is batting .233 with one home run, 28 RBI, 34 runs scored and 32 stolen bases across 82 games. Nunez needed a solid game at the plate, and his first home run of the season delivered. The speedy infielder is hitting just .167 over his last seven games with nine strikeouts.

author: Jesse Garcia
title: Andres Chaparro cashes in with rare long ball in Boston
desc: Andres Chaparro went 1-for-2 in a win over the Red Sox with a home run, one run scored, and two RBI.
impact: After Wednesday's win over the Red Sox, Chaparro is batting .192 with one home run, seven RBI, nine runs scored, 11 walks and 14 strikeouts across 26 games. As a platoon player, Chaparro does not offer much fantasy value.

author: Jesse Garcia
title: James Wood mashes, drives in three as Nats rout Boston
desc: James Wood went 2-for-4 in the win over the Red Sox with a home run, two walks, two runs scored, three RBI and one strikeout.
impact: After Wednesday's win, Wood is slashing .265/.389/.522 with 22 home runs, 55 RBI, 75 runs scored and 13 stolen bases across 88 games. Wood seems to be coming out of a bit of a slump over the last few weeks, now hitting .276 with two home runs and six RBI over his last seven games.

author: Nate Miller
title: Ozzie Albies homers, drives in a pair Wednesday night
desc: Ozzie Albies went 2-for-4 with a solo homer, a double, two RBI, and two runs scored in Wednesday's 5-1 win over the Cardinals.
impact: Albies continues to be one bat that keeps coming up with big hits for the recently slumping Braves. The switch-hitting All-Star has driven in two runs each of the last two nights and in three of his last five games. Surprisingly, Albies only has four hits overall in that span, but he's making them count. For the season, Albies is up to 13 homers, 15 doubles, 48 RBI, and 53 runs through 84 games.

author: Jesse Garcia
title: Dean Kremer cruises past White Sox in efficient six-inning win
desc: Dean Kremer allowed one earned run on four hits and one walk while striking out four over six innings in Wednesday's win over the White Sox.
impact: After the win, he owns a 3.18 ERA and 0.88 WHIP with a 1-1 record through three starts. Kremer looked sharp in his return from the injured list, and he will look to keep it going in his next scheduled start against the Cubs.

author: Jesse Garcia
title: Leody Taveras finally flashes some pop in lopsided win
desc: Taveras went 1-for-3 in a win over the White Sox with a home run, one walk, two runs scored, one RBI and one stolen base.
impact: After Wednesday's win, Taveras is batting .248 with three home runs, 31 RBI, 32 runs scored and 10 stolen bases across 75 games. Taveras is just 3-for-22 in his last seven games as he current struggles at the plate lately limit his fantasy value.

author: Jesse Garcia
title: Tyler O'Neill goes deep in limited chances vs. White Sox
desc: Tyler O'Neill went 1-for-2 in a 6-1 win over the White Sox with a solo home run, one run scored, one RBI, a walk and a strikeout.
impact: After Wednesday's win, O'Neill is batting .187 with three homers, nine RBI, 17 runs scored and one steal across 52 games. Despite a better run at the plate as of late, the veteran is not fantasy viable right now.

author: Nate Miller
title: Reynaldo Lopez handles Cardinals in Wednesday's win
desc: Reynaldo Lopez allowed one run on just two hits and one walk while striking out six over five innings in Wednesday's 5-1 win against the Cardinals.
impact: Lopez's second turn since returning to the Atlanta rotation was arguably his best all-around effort of the season. The veteran righty surrendered a single tally in the opening frame, but that was it, as he shut the Cardinals down over the next four, needing only 69 pitches to get through five innings. Lopez is now sporting a 3.31 ERA and 21.0 K% through 20 appearances (seven starts) on the season. He will draw his next start Monday against the Mets.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Max Meyer picks up loss Wednesday
desc: Max Meyer allowed five runs (one earned) on six hits and no walks while striking out five across six innings in Wednesday's 6-3 loss to the Colorado Rockies.
impact: While Meyer picked up the loss, he allowed just one earned run in the contest and has now allowed two earned runs or fewer in six straight games. Following the outing, he owns a 2.53 ERA and 1.11 WHIP with 112 strikeouts across a career-high 103 innings. His next scheduled start is on Tuesday against the Seattle Mariners.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Joe Mack hits inside-the-park homer Wednesday
desc: Joe Mack went 1-for-1 with an inside-the-park home run in Wednesday's 6-3 loss to the Colorado Rockies.
impact: Mack did not draw the start behind the plate on Wednesday, but came in as a pinch-hitter for Brian Navarreto and took full advantage of the opportunity, using his legs to leg out his sixth home run of the season. In 44 games this season, he owns a .256/.313/.429 slash line.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Shane McClanahan pitches six scoreless innings Wednesday
desc: Shane McClanahan gave up three hits and no walks while striking out four across six scoreless innings in Wednesday's 4-0 victory over the Kansas City Royals.
impact: McClanahan delivered one of his best starts of the season, giving up just three singles and not walking a batter for the first time since his May 31 start against the Los Angeles Angels. While he had a rough June with a 5.79 ERA, he started July on a strong note. He owns a 3.05 ERA and 1.17 WHIP with 77 strikeouts across 79.2 innings this season. He'll look to deliver another quality start in his next scheduled outing on Monday against the New York Yankees.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Cedric Mullins II blasts one over fence Wednesday
desc: Cedric Mullins II went 2-for-4 with a home run, one run scored and two RBI in Wednesday's 4-0 victory over the Kansas City Royals.
impact: Mullins' homer came in the sixth inning off Seth Lugo, giving the Tampa Bay Rays a 3-0 lead. He's been excellent as of late, riding a six-game hitting streak and going yard three times during that span.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Junior Caminero homers in sixth-straight game Wednesday
desc: Junior Caminero went 1-for-4 with a two-run home run in Wednesday's 4-0 victory over the Kansas City Royals.
impact: Caminero swung at the first pitch he saw from Seth Lugo in the first inning and belted a 425-foot home run over the left-field fence. He's now homered in six straight games, matching the franchise record set by Carlos Peña in 2010. Wednesday's blast also made him the youngest player since at least 1900 to homer in six consecutive games. He'll look to extend the streak on Thursday in the series finale against the Royals, with Stephen Kolek on the mound.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Michael Conforto mashes two homers Wednesday
desc: Michael Conforto went 3-for-4 with two home runs, two walks, four runs scored and four RBI in Wednesday's 23-3 win over the San Diego Padres.
impact: Conforto drew the start for the third time over the Chicago Cubs' last five games and took full advantage, posting his first multi-homer game of the year. After struggling in June with a .154/.214/.256 slash line, he kicked off July with a bang. While he's seen limited playing time this year, he's been great overall, hitting .248 with an .847 OPS across 121 at-bats.
